nodes.title: End-to-End Business Flow Model
nodes.intro_md: The flow crosses three ownership boundaries: **storefront** (order intent and payment), **platform inventory** (reservations and the sellable view) and **WMS/SC2P** (physical stock and outbound execution). Every stage is listed with the inventory effect it must produce, so each stage becomes a directly testable assertion rather than a narrative.

children.title: Stage-level failure modes (must be covered by F cases)
bullets: Stage 3 fails: reserve times out or WMS says insufficient -> order must be REJECTED, no ledger entry left behind.
Stage 4 fails after money moved: payment callback lost or gateway error -> order must not stay PENDING_PAYMENT silently; reconciliation job must find and repair it.
Stage 5 fails: SO push rejected or ACK lost -> order must not be double-pushed; retry must be idempotent by SO id.
Stage 6 out-of-order: ship notice arriving before allocation ACK must not corrupt state.
Stage 8 partial: only the returned quantity may be restored; the rest stays sold.
Stage 10 abnormal close: any non-terminal order closed by a job must release its reservation first.

nodes.title: Order State Machine
nodes.intro_md: 14 states, five of them terminal, and an explicit guard (or an explicit refusal) on every transition. Each transition lists a guard that is enforced before the transition runs. An omitted guard is how a refund gets issued against an already-shipped order, so the guards act as test oracles.

nodes.title: Inventory State Model
nodes.intro_md: Four buckets (on_hand, available, reserved, frozen) plus a cumulative sold counter, six invariants and one append-only ledger. The invariants are what make inventory testable: every case asserts them **before and after**, and the reconciliation jobs assert them continuously.

rows: Inbound receipt, outbound confirm, return receipt, ADJUST
Held by non-terminal unpaid/pending orders (has a TTL)
Blocked from sale (QC hold, damage, channel lock)
Cumulative deducted quantity (ledger concept, not a bucket)
Configured buffer never exposed to sale

tables.title: Core invariant (asserted by every inventory test case and by the reconciliation job)
rows: sum(ledger.qty for type=RESERVE - type=RELEASE - type=DEDUCT) == reserved
on_hand == snapshot_on_hand + sum(RESTORE + INBOUND - DEDUCT - ADJUST_out)
Platform and WMS disagree on physical stock
every mutation has exactly one ledger entry with a unique idempotency key
every reservation is resolvable: it ends in DEDUCT or RELEASE within its TTL

children.title: Interface contracts that must be frozen before test execution
bullets: Signed OpenAPI/JSON-Schema for E1, E8 and E9, published to the test team and validated by contract tests.
Message schema version field on every MQ message, with a documented compatibility rule (additive only within a major version).
Published error-code dictionary shared by platform, WMS and gateway, including retryable vs non-retryable classification.
Clock-skew tolerance declared (+/-5min) and enforced identically on both sides.
A mock WMS/SC2P with a fault-injection switch per message type, so every E-case can be driven deterministically.

nodes.title: Consistency Boundaries and Reconciliation Points
nodes.intro_md: The system cannot make every boundary strongly consistent, and trying to do so is what produces overselling defects. Each boundary is assigned a mode, an authoritative side, a conflict rule and a reconciliation cadence.

tables.title: Consistency boundaries
rows: Single transaction on the inventory row (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE / Redis-Lua atomic decrement with DB fallback)
Second concurrent request loses; available never < 0
Unique index on pay_no + state guard in the same transaction
Duplicate callback is a no-op; state machine guard wins over the callback
At-least-once delivery (synchronous ACK with MQ-backed retry) + idempotent SO apply keyed on so_id
WMS allocation is authoritative for warehouse/shortage; platform never re-pushes a live SO
Platform must accept shipment even if the allocation ACK was lost (out-of-order tolerance)
WMS for on_hand, platform for available
Version-guarded snapshot apply; delta events ordered by event_ts
WMS on_hand always wins; an in-flight reservation is never canceled by a snapshot, the drift is reported instead
Idempotent RESTORE keyed on rma_no + qc_seq
restore only on QC PASS and only for the received quantity
Unique index on refund_no + state guard
refund callback for an unknown/closed order goes to manual queue, never auto-revives the order

tables.title: Reconciliation points and cadence
rows: alert if DLQ > 0; manual approval above 100 messages
orders non-terminal longer than stage SLA
alert; auto-compensate where a safe rule exists
Inventory diff job: platform (available+reserved+frozen) vs WMS (on_hand - safety_stock)
classify A/B/C and auto-repair A, page on ratio breach
Full stock snapshot reconciliation (E4) + three-way order/payment/shipment recon
generate ADJUST with recon_batch_id; publish audit report
freeze the SKU from sale + P0 alert until repaired

children.title: Why these modes (design rationale to defend in review)
bullets: C1 is strong because an oversell is unrecoverable: you cannot un-sell 200 units of a 100-unit SKU.
C4 is eventual and must tolerate the lost-ACK case, because the physical shipment already happened; refusing the ship notice corrupts customer-visible reality.
C5 lets WMS win on on_hand but never lets a snapshot silently delete a live reservation, otherwise a bulk sync becomes an oversell machine.
C2 and C7 are strong because a duplicated payment effect moves real money and shows up as a chargeback.
Every eventual boundary carries a named reconciliation point and a numeric tolerance; a boundary without one is treated as an untested defect.

No request fails with a 5xx caused by contention handling

children.title: Quantity boundaries: zero, negative, fractional, over the per-order cap, and exactly equal to available
precondition: SKU-A available = 10, max_per_order configured = 5
steps: Read responses, order table and ledger
expected: Invalid quantities are rejected by validation with a documented code and create no ledger entry
qty = 6 exceeds max_per_order -> rejected with QUANTITY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
qty = 5, exactly at the cap, succeeds and leaves available at 5 - never negative and never an off-by-one

children.title: Payment callback and the timeout-close job race at the same instant
precondition: Order O1 PENDING_PAYMENT with the 30-minute deadline about to expire
steps: Trigger the close job and deliver the payment callback within the same second, both orders of arrival
Read the final state, the ledger and the payment record
expected: Exactly one of the two outcomes is applied: either PAID with a DEDUCT, or CLOSED with a RELEASE
The loser is handled explicitly: an unpaid close must not strand a real payment (it is routed to auto-refund), and a paid order must not be closed
Never a state where money was taken and the reservation was released without a refund path
Ledger has exactly one of DEDUCT or RELEASE, never both

children.title: Timeout boundary precision: 29:59 stays open, 30:01 is closed
precondition: Two orders created with controlled created_at values
steps: Run the close job at created_at + 29:59 and at + 30:01
expected: The 29:59 order remains PENDING_PAYMENT and keeps its reservation
The 30:01 order becomes CLOSED and releases it
No off-by-one mass release of live orders

children.title: Partial shipment does not change sold quantities
precondition: Order O2 PAID, three lines, all deducted
steps: Emit a ship notice covering one line
Read the ledger, sold and order status
expected: Status = PARTIAL_SHIPPED; no additional DEDUCT and no RESTORE
sold remains the full order quantity
Per-line shipped quantity tracked for later reconciliation

children.title: Split shipment across two warehouses produces two packages under one order
precondition: Order O3 allocated from WH01 and WH02
steps: Emit two ship notices, one per warehouse package
expected: One order, two packages, two tracking numbers, no duplicate order rows
Status reaches SHIPPED only after both packages ship
Ledger is per warehouse and balances per warehouse as well as in aggregate

children.title: Partial return restores only the returned quantity
precondition: Order O4 SIGNED with 3 units; sold = 3, on_hand = 7
steps: Create an RMA for 1 unit and emit E7 with QC PASS
expected: on_hand 7 -> 8, available +1, sold 3 -> 2
The other 2 units stay sold and remain reconcilable
Exactly one RESTORE entry with the RMA key

children.title: Return that fails QC is not restored to sellable stock
precondition: Order O4 SIGNED; a returned unit is damaged
steps: Read inventory, ledger and the reason record
expected: No RESTORE occurs; sold and on_hand are unchanged
The RMA is closed with a QC_FAIL reason and an audit record
The returned physical unit is accounted for as frozen/non-sellable rather than silently lost

children.title: Duplicate return receipt for one RMA restores stock only once
precondition: One RMA exists in RETURNING state
steps: Deliver the identical E7 message five times
Read ledger, inventory and the RMA
expected: Exactly one RESTORE entry; on_hand increases by the received quantity once
The extra deliveries return success but mutate nothing
available never exceeds the physically returned quantity

children.title: Oversized payload / very large order
precondition: Construct an order with 999 lines and with a single line of qty 99999
expected: Behavior matches the published limits (accepted, or rejected with a documented size code) and is deterministic
A rejected oversized order leaves zero ledger residue and no partial reservation
If accepted, all lines are reserved atomically or not at all

children.title: Duplicate submit of the same cart (double click / retry) yields one order
precondition: A valid cart with a client idempotency key
steps: Fire the same createOrder request 10 times concurrently with the identical key
Read the orders table, ledger and the payment intents
expected: Exactly one order_no is created and returned to all callers
Exactly one RESERVE and one payment intent
No duplicate reservation, therefore no leaked stock

children.title: Post-flash-sale conservation: nothing created, nothing lost
precondition: Flash sale of 500 units completes and all timers have run
steps: Read inventory, ledger and the order list
Run the conservation checks (I1, I3, I4)
expected: available = 0, reserved = 0, sold = 500, on_hand = 0
Every reservation resolved into DEDUCT or RELEASE; zero orphans
Ledger sums match the bucket values exactly; the 24-hour reconciliation reports zero unexplained diff

children.title: Cancel or refund a SHIPPED order is refused by the state guard
precondition: Order O1 is SHIPPED with stock deducted
expected: Both are rejected with ORDER_STATE_ILLEGAL and no inventory or money movement
The only permitted path remains the return/RMA journey
The rejection is logged with the order_no for audit

nodes.title: Critical API and Contract Validation
nodes.intro_md: Contract-level coverage: request validation, error-code semantics, callback write-back fields and the boundary between what the client may assert and what the server must recompute.

children.title: createOrder request-field validation
precondition: A contract-test harness driven from the published JSON Schema
steps: Submit variants: missing skuId, qty as a string, qty negative, field exceeding maxLength, illegal status enum, unknown extra field, malformed JSON, wrong content-type
expected: Each invalid request returns 4xx with a field-level error path and the documented code
No 5xx, no partial order, no ledger entry for any invalid request
Optional fields are absent-tolerant while required fields are strictly enforced

children.title: createOrder idempotency key is required and honoured
precondition: Two calls, one with a missing key and one reusing a valid key
steps: Call twice with the same key but a slightly different body
expected: Missing key -> rejected with IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED (documented decision, not silent acceptance)
Same key returns the original order_no and creates no second order or reservation
Same key with a different body is rejected as a conflict rather than silently ignored

children.title: Authentication and replay protection on write APIs
precondition: Known credentials plus a captured, previously accepted request
steps: Replay with a missing signature, an invalid signature, a timestamp 10 minutes old, and a reused nonce
expected: All rejections with 401/403 and a documented code
Zero state change and zero ledger entry for rejected calls
Timestamp and nonce windows enforced identically on platform and WMS sides

children.title: Authorization isolation between tenants/users
precondition: User A's token and user B's order id
steps: Read, cancel and refund B's order with A's token
Attempt admin-only inventory adjustment with a normal user token
expected: 403 for every cross-user access; the resource existence is not leaked
Admin-only mutation requires the admin role and a reason code
Denials are audited

children.title: Error-code contract: business errors are 4xx with documented codes
precondition: A catalog of known business-error triggers (insufficient stock, illegal state, duplicate request, off-shelf SKU)
steps: Compare the returned code/message against the published dictionary
expected: Every business error maps to the documented code and an appropriate 4xx
No 5xx for expected business conditions
Error responses contain no stack traces, SQL, internal hostnames or PII

children.title: Client-supplied price or quantity is never trusted
precondition: A crafted createOrder request carrying amount = 0.01 for a 100.00 SKU
steps: Read the stored order amount and the payment intent
expected: The server recomputes the amount from SKU and promotion rules
A tampered amount is either ignored or rejected with PRICE_MISMATCH, never honoured
The amount stored equals the amount charged in the later payment callback

children.title: Payment callback write-back contract
precondition: A signed callback template with every documented field
steps: Deliver an amount mismatch, an unknown order_no, a bad signature, a missing pay_no and a duplicate pay_no
expected: Amount mismatch -> rejected, no state change, alert raised, callback acknowledged safely
Unknown order_no -> routed to the manual/exception queue, never auto-creating an order
Bad signature -> 401 with no mutation; duplicate pay_no -> idempotent success
Every callback outcome is visible in a metric with the reject reason

children.title: WMS ship-notice write-back contract
precondition: A schema-valid and several schema-invalid ship notices
steps: Deliver: valid, missing tracking_no, illegal tracking_no format, package count not matching the shipped quantity sum, unknown so_id
Inspect order state, DLQ and alerts
expected: Valid notice applies fully and is idempotent per package
Invalid notices go to the DLQ with a reason and cause no state change
Unknown so_id is parked and alerted rather than creating a new order

children.title: Stock synchronization message schema and version guard
precondition: E4/E5 messages with a missing version field, a future-major version and a wrong type on qty
steps: Read applied version, inventory and the DLQ
expected: A missing or unsupported version is rejected rather than guessed
Type errors are rejected at the boundary with a schema-error reason
Every accepted message is recorded with its version for traceability

children.title: Query API limits and encoding
precondition: A large result set and adversarial inputs
steps: Request page_size = 0, -1, 100000; an unknown sort field; SQL/HTML fragments and emoji in address and remark; a 5,000-character remark
expected: Pagination is bounded by the documented cap and returns 4xx beyond it
Sort/field names are whitelisted; unknown values rejected
Unicode and emoji are stored and returned round-trip correctly; injection attempts are neutralized with no data disclosure

children.title: Cancel/refund API validation and guards
precondition: Orders in PENDING_PAYMENT, PAID and SHIPPED states
steps: Cancel/refund each with: no reason code, an illegal reason code, a missing order_no, no permission
expected: State guard runs before any side effect
Reason code is validated against an enum and persisted
Permission failures return 403 without revealing order details

children.title: Sensitive-data masking in responses, logs and messages
precondition: An order carrying a full phone number, a detailed address and an ID number
steps: Read the order via the API, the admin console and a raw log export; inspect the SO push payload and MQ messages
expected: Storefront/admin responses mask phone and ID; the full value is returned only to an authorized owner in an approved field
Logs contain no unmasked PII (verified by a log scan in CI)
Outbound WMS messages carry only the fields the warehouse needs, not the full customer record

children.title: No internal-field leakage from storefront responses
precondition: A normal order plus an order in an internal failure state
steps: Diff the response payload against the public contract schema
expected: No cost price, supplier id, raw WMS payload, internal flags or exception stack appears
Contract tests fail the build when a non-contracted field is added

nodes.title: Performance
nodes.intro_md: Every target is stated as a number under a specific traffic shape, so it is measurable rather than descriptive. The controlling constraint is the flash-sale profile: high contention against small inventory.

tables.title: Performance targets (must be met at 1.5x the projected peak)
rows: Oversell must remain exactly 0 at any error rate
Public endpoint, must absorb gateway retries
Cache must not serve stale availability at the moment of reserve
Backlog must not exceed 10k at any sample
Excludes WMS human pick time; measures platform-side latency only

tables.title: Load model and pass conditions
rows: All latency targets met; resource headroom >= 40%
Latency and error targets met; no queue growth trend
Step to 20k QPS in 1s, fresh 500-unit SKU per cycle
Zero oversell; no negative bucket; exactly 500 successes in the first cycle and every later attempt rejected with STOCK_INSUFFICIENT; baseline latency recovered within 60s
No memory leak (RSS growth < 5%), no connection leak, GC pauses bounded, error rate stable
The system degrades by rejecting business requests, not by corrupting state: zero invariant violations at the knee
Consumer lag recovers to <= 30s within 15min after the surge ends

children.title: Flash-sale burst causes zero oversell and zero invariant violation
precondition: Perf environment, 500-unit SKU, load generator ready with a synchronized start
steps: Continuously sample available/reserved/sold and the latency histogram
expected: No sample shows a negative bucket or available + reserved + frozen != on_hand - safety_stock
Exactly 500 orders succeed; every later attempt in the same cycle is rejected with STOCK_INSUFFICIENT, never a 5xx
Error responses are business rejections, not 5xx; latency targets met

children.title: Sustained peak does not degrade into a queue collapse
precondition: Perf environment at production-like topology
steps: Track queue depth, consumer lag and p99 over time
expected: Latency and error targets hold for the whole hold period
No monotonic growth in backlog or thread pool saturation
Auto-scaling (if configured) stabilizes without flapping

children.title: Eight-hour soak shows no leak and no slow drift
precondition: 1.2x peak, steady mixed traffic with sync traffic included
steps: Sample RSS, GC pauses, connection pool, ledger/DB growth, inventory divergence hourly
expected: Memory growth bounded (< 5%); no FD/connection leak
Inventory diff does not grow with time
Error rate and latency stable between hour 1 and hour 8

children.title: Breakpoint behavior fails closed, never corrupts
precondition: Ramp load past the system knee
steps: Increase load until the system degrades
Inspect state and error taxonomy at the knee
expected: Degradation appears as explicit business/system rejections with retryable codes
Zero state corruption: no oversell, no negative bucket, no partial ledger entry
Recovery to normal latency without a restart once load recedes

nodes.title: Reliability
nodes.intro_md: Reliability is specified as concrete mechanisms with parameters, together with the chaos scenarios that exercise them. The order/inventory boundary is designed to be at-least-once and idempotent, so 'exactly once' is never assumed anywhere.

tables.title: Reliability mechanisms and parameters
rows: All outbound calls (E1, E8) and all consumers
Max 3 attempts, exponential backoff 1s/4s/16s with jitter; only idempotent operations retried
Retries never produce a second effect; attempt count visible in metrics
Timeout produces a documented retryable error, not a hang; no thread starvation under a slow dependency
Open when error rate > 50% over a 20s window; open for 30s; half-open probe 1 request
During a WMS outage, order creation degrades predictably (fail fast or queue per policy) instead of stalling
Order, inventory and sync thread/connection pools
A WMS slowdown must not exhaust the pool used by payment callbacks
Serve last-known-good with an explicit staleness marker; never invent availability
No stale read is allowed to authorize a reserve that violates the invariant
Scheduled sweep with per-class SLA and idempotency key
Each seeded drift is detected and repaired exactly once within its SLA
Dead-letter with reason; replay requires approval above 100 messages
Replay after a fix applies correctly and only once
Late events are discarded; state matches the newest event
A 6-minute skew is rejected; a 4-minute skew is accepted

tables.title: Chaos and recovery drills (run in TEST/STAGE before release)
rows: Orders fail fast or queue per policy; no state corruption; alerts fire; after restore, backlog drains and reconciliation is clean
No message loss for persisted messages; consumers resume; duplicates are absorbed idempotently
Cache rebuilds from the ledger; no oversell during the rebuild window
At most the transaction in flight is lost; no partially applied ledger entry
Signature validation rejects out-of-window messages with a clear reason; no silent data loss
Add 5s latency to the WMS client
Circuit breaker opens; order creation fails fast instead of timing out under load
All duplicates are no-ops; no drift; ledger row count unchanged
Fail half of a 1,000-message bulk sync batch
Successful half applies; failed half lands in the DLQ and is replayable

children.title: Seeded drift classes are all detected and compensated within SLA
precondition: Five deliberate drifts seeded: paid-but-not-deducted, shipped-but-not-deducted, closed-but-reservation-alive, return-received-but-not-restored, lost callback
steps: Track detection time, repair time and the ledger entries produced
expected: All five are detected within the declared window and repaired exactly once
Each repair leaves an ADJUST/compensation ledger entry with a reason code and batch id
Invariants I1, I3 and I4 hold after the sweep; no drift recurs

children.title: Circuit breaker and fail-fast under a WMS outage
precondition: WMS mock switchable to an outage
steps: Restore the WMS and observe recovery
expected: Circuit opens within the declared window; order creation returns the documented retryable/queue response rather than hanging
Payment callbacks continue to be processed (bulkhead verified)
After restore, the breaker closes, the backlog drains and reconciliation reports zero unexplained diff

children.title: Timeout and retry produce no duplicate effect
precondition: A dependency configured to accept the request and then time out on the response
steps: Trigger the retry path for E1 (SO push) and for the reserve call
Compare the effective apply count on the dependency with the platform ledger
expected: The dependency applies the operation once; the platform ledger matches
Retry attempts and outcomes are visible in metrics; the DLQ is empty after the fixed path is used

children.title: Message-order guarantees hold under a reordering storm
precondition: A stream of E5 events plus E2/E3 pairs shuffled with duplicates
steps: Compare final state with the expected final state computed from the source of truth
expected: Final state matches the expectation exactly
Duplicates and reordered messages leave no residue
DLQ is empty and the late-message metric reflects the discarded stale events only

nodes.title: Observability
nodes.intro_md: Each consistency guarantee is backed by a metric, an owning team and an alert, surfaced on a dashboard. Every metric below carries an owner, a threshold and an action, so the on-call runbook is testable.

tables.title: Required metrics
rows: Absolute difference between platform(available+reserved+frozen) and WMS(on_hand - safety_stock), divided by WMS(on_hand), per warehouse
The single best indicator that sync has silently broken
Number of times available went below 0 or an order was accepted beyond stock
Successful reserves / attempts, with reason breakdown
Distinguishes real contention from a broken dependency
Non-terminal orders older than their stage SLA, by stage
Compensation jobs that repaired within SLA / attempts
Histogram of time in each state
Finds the stage where reality stalls
Proves the ordering guard is real and not silently dropping live data
Last line of defense for inventory truth

tables.title: Alerts, severity and required action
rows: Page on-call; freeze the SKU from sale; open an incident; start the drift repair runbook (S5)
Identify the warehouse and SKU set; run the hourly recon out of band; decide auto-repair vs manual
Check the WMS deduct endpoint and the compensation sweep; verify no paid-but-not-deducted backlog
Check consumer health and the broker; scale consumers; verify no DLQ growth
Group by stage; run the stage-specific compensation job; identify the blocked dependency
Inspect reasons; fix the contract break; replay with approval
Reject the write, page, freeze the SKU, escalate to the data-repair runbook
Check key rotation and the timestamp window; confirm no credential drift between sides

tables.title: Logging, tracing and audit requirements
rows: JSON with trace_id, order_no, sku_id, warehouse_code, message_id, idempotency_key, latency; no PII (verified by a CI log scan)
Every inventory mutation is an immutable ledger row with before/after values, source (API/MQ/JOB), reason code and operator for manual work
One trace spans createOrder -> reserve -> payment callback -> deduct -> SO push -> ship notice, so out-of-order cases are diagnosable
The WMS message_id and the platform order_no appear together in logs on both sides of every boundary
Business funnel (order/pay/ship/sign), sync health (backlog, diff ratio, DLQ), compensation board (drift by class, MTTR), peak-load board (QPS, p99, error taxonomy)
Every manual repair records operator, ticket, before/after, reason code and a reversal path; adjustments are never a raw UPDATE
Metrics 13 months, traces 7 days, ledger indefinite, audit indefinite

children.title: Every alert in the catalog fires on a synthetically injected condition
precondition: Alert rules deployed to the test environment with the production thresholds
steps: Inject each condition in turn (oversell simulation, sync stall, DLQ growth, stuck orders, lag)
Measure detection latency and check the notification content
expected: Each alert fires within its declared detection window with the correct severity
The payload names the SKU/warehouse/order and links to the relevant dashboard
No alert storm: a single incident produces one notification per severity, not per event

children.title: Inventory diff ratio reflects a real divergence within one cycle
precondition: A synthetic divergence of 0.1% introduced for one warehouse
steps: Wait for the hourly diff job
Read the metric, the alert and the report
expected: The metric reports the divergence within the declared cadence
The alert fires at the configured threshold
The report lists the SKUs and deltas for triage

children.title: Trace continuity across the storefront-WMS boundary
precondition: A single order driven end-to-end with the WMS mock
steps: Collect the trace ids for createOrder, reserve, callback, deduct, SO push, ship notice
Check the logs on both sides
expected: One searchable correlation id links the whole journey
Out-of-order arrivals are visible in the trace with timestamps proving the sequence
No PII appears in the traced payloads

children.title: Stuck-order detection covers every non-terminal stage
precondition: One order artifically stalled in each non-terminal state
expected: Every stalled order is reported with its stage and dwell time
Grouping by stage matches the injected set exactly (no false negatives)
Alerts respect the threshold and do not fire on healthy orders

nodes.title: Security
nodes.intro_md: The order/inventory surface is where money and personal data meet, so the tests target authorization boundaries, callback authenticity, price tampering and PII exposure rather than generic vulnerability scanning.

tables.title: Security requirements and verification
rows: HMAC-SHA256 request signing plus timestamp (+/-5min) and a single-use nonce for all write APIs; mTLS between platform and WMS where supported
Replay, skew and tamper tests return 401/403 with no side effect (F4-03)
RBAC with tenant isolation; inventory ADJUST and refunds are privileged operations
Cross-user and cross-role access attempts all return 403 (F4-04); privileged ops require two-person approval above a configured quantity
Phone, name, address and ID encrypted at rest; masked in logs, dashboards, storefront responses and error messages; never in metrics labels
Automated PII scan of logs and responses in CI (F4-12)
Server-side recomputation of amount; client values are advisory only
Tampered amount is rejected or ignored, never charged (F4-06)
Parameterized queries, output encoding, whitelisted sort/fields, size limits on address/remark
Injection and oversized-input suite passes with no data disclosure (F4-10)
Idempotency keys prevent duplicate orders; rate limiting on order create and coupon endpoints
Duplicate-submit storm yields one order (F3-14); rate limiter returns 429 without affecting legitimate users
Keys in a secret store, rotated on a schedule, never in code, config or logs; per-environment keys
Rotation test: both sides accept the new key after rotation with no downtime; no secret appears in the repo or logs
Every state change and every manual adjustment is attributable
Audit query returns operator, ticket, before/after for each manual repair
Known-CVE scan of images and dependencies gates the release
No high/critical CVEs with an available fix at release time

children.title: Callback authenticity cannot be bypassed
precondition: Captured valid callbacks plus a signing key in the test store
steps: Attempt: no signature, wrong key, tampered amount, replayed nonce, expired timestamp, body/header mismatch
expected: Every attempt is rejected with no state mutation and an audit log entry
The rejection reason distinguishes auth failure from contract failure
Legitimate callbacks continue to succeed during the attack window (no denial of service from the guard)

children.title: Privileged inventory adjustment requires authorization and leaves an audit trail
precondition: A normal user token and an admin token
steps: Attempt an ADJUST with the normal token
Perform one with the admin token and a reason code
expected: Normal token -> 403 with no change
Admin adjustment adds a ledger row with operator, ticket, reason and before/after values
A reversal produces a second auditable entry rather than deleting the first

children.title: No PII in logs, metrics or outbound messages
precondition: An order carrying a full phone number, address and ID
steps: Scan logs, metric labels, traces and all outbound WMS/gateway payloads
expected: Zero unmasked PII occurrences (regex plus a checksum-based scan for ID numbers)
The outbound WMS message contains only warehouse-relevant fields
The CI gate fails the build if the scan regresses

children.title: Release gate: dependency and image scan
precondition: The release candidate images and the SBOM
steps: Run the CVE scan and the secrets scan
expected: No high/critical vulnerability with an available fix ships with the release
No secret or key material is present in the repository or the image layers
Findings are recorded with an owner and an accepted-risk decision where deferred

nodes.title: Recoverability
nodes.intro_md: Recoverability is verified through drills with explicit targets rather than left to written procedures alone. Each drill has a target and each repair path has one tested procedure.

tables.title: Failure drills and targets
rows: RTO <= 15min, RPO = 0 for order and payment data
Order count and ledger sums identical before and after; no partially applied entry
Restore the latest backup and replay to a chosen timestamp
Sandbox totals match the production report for that timestamp; documented restore duration
No order or inventory corruption; all messages recovered or explicitly rejected
Zero unexplained diff after recovery; DLQ drained or triaged
Inventory correctness preserved with the cache cold
No oversell during the rebuild window; latency recovers within 5min
Roll back the last release within the window
Schema-compatible rollback verified; feature flags allow a behavioral rollback without a deploy
Recalibrate the platform view from the WMS source of truth
ADJUST ledger entries with reason RECALIBRATION; invariants hold; an approval record exists
Rebuild the SKU's quantities from the ledger
Rebuilt values match the pre-computed expectation; the SKU returns from frozen to sellable

tables.title: Data-repair process (one procedure, three classes)
rows: A reconciliation job or an alert identifies a divergence (never a customer complaint)
Class A: safe to auto-repair (e.g. a lost RELEASE). Class B: semi-automatic, needs a human approval. Class C: manual investigation (money or PII involved)
Freeze the affected SKU from sale if the divergence could cause an oversell; stop the affected job if it is amplifying the drift
Apply the correction as an ADJUST ledger entry with a reason code and a batch id. Never a raw UPDATE. Idempotent and replayable
Automated for A, on-call for B/C
Re-run the invariant checks and the reconciliation; confirm the diff ratio returns below tolerance
Audit entry with operator, ticket, before/after, reason and a reversal path; post-mortem for Class B/C

children.title: Database failover loses no order and no ledger entry
precondition: A production-like environment with a replica and the failover mechanism configured
steps: Let the failover complete, then compare state
expected: RTO within target; order and payment RPO = 0
No partially applied ledger entry and no orphan reservation
Invariants hold after recovery; the reconciliation reports zero unexplained diff

children.title: Point-in-time restore reproduces known totals
precondition: A backup plus an agreed reference timestamp and its reported totals
steps: Restore into a sandbox and replay to the reference timestamp
Compare orders, payments and ledger sums
expected: Totals match the reference report exactly
Restore duration is recorded against the target
The procedure is executable by an on-call engineer from the runbook alone (no tribal knowledge)

children.title: Stock recalibration from the WMS source of truth is safe and audited
precondition: A deliberately divergent SKU/warehouse
steps: Run the recalibration procedure with an approval record
Inspect the ledger, invariants and the SKU's sellable state
expected: Divergence is corrected with reason-coded ADJUST entries carrying the batch id
Invariants hold; the SKU returns to sellable if previously frozen
The approval record names the approver and the ticket

children.title: Rollback of a release is verified, not assumed
precondition: The release candidate plus its predecessor image and the feature flags
steps: Roll back to the predecessor and disable the new flags
Run the smoke and consistency checks
expected: Rollback completes within the window without a schema migration
Order/inventory consistency is preserved across the rollback
Any message produced by the new version remains consumable by the old one (schema compatibility verified)

nodes.title: Dedicated: Inventory Synchronization Consistency
nodes.intro_md: This section is the cross-layer view of the requirement that matters most. It restates the guarantee, lists the defect classes it must prevent, defines who wins each conflict, and states the exact evidence that proves the guarantee holds.

tables.title: S4.1 The guarantee, stated as falsifiable claims
rows: The platform never authorizes a sale it cannot fulfil from sellable stock
A successful order exists while available is negative, or oversell_count > 0
Flash-sale case F3-03 and Q1-01 with exactly the configured quantity sold and zero negative samples
Every physical movement is reflected exactly once in the ledger
A duplicate or replayed message changes a bucket twice, or a movement leaves no ledger row
Idempotency suite F2-08..F2-10, F2-17, F3-12; ledger sum checks I3/I4
Platform and WMS converge to the same truth within one reconciliation cycle
diff ratio above tolerance persists across two cycles
Hourly diff job with a 24h zero-unexplained-diff report (F3-15, Q3-02)
No reservation can outlive its purpose
A terminal order still holds reserved stock after the TTL
Reservation TTL guard case F2-19 and invariant I6
Every divergence has an automated, audited repair path
A drift is found with no job that can repair it, or a repair is done by a raw UPDATE
Compensation sweep Q2-01 with reason-coded ADJUST entries

tables.title: S4.2 Defect classes this section must prevent (and the case that catches each)
rows: Non-atomic check-then-update, cached availability used as authority, retry without idempotency
Redelivered DEDUCT or duplicate payment callback
Deduct call failed after payment succeeded, with no compensation
Cancel/close path missed, or a job failed after the state change
Sellable stock artificially reduced, lost sales
Restored stock that was never returned
Bulk sync applied without a version guard
Phantom stock or deleted live reservations
Ship notice applied before allocation, or an old delta applied late
Consumer died, backlog grew, nobody noticed
No reconciliation, or a repair that cannot be replayed

tables.title: S4.3 Conflict resolution rules (who wins, and why)
rows: Physical stock: platform view vs WMS on_hand
WMS is the source of truth for on_hand
The platform records the drift and raises an alert; it never silently rewrites live reservations
A reserve is authorized by the transactional ledger, never by a cached read
The cache serves reads only and is marked stale when being rebuilt
Order state: state machine vs late callback
A terminal or later state rejects the older event, and the event is not lost, it is routed to a queue
The callback is acknowledged to prevent a retry storm
Message ordering: two delta events for the same SKU
The older event is discarded and counted in a metric
A bulk snapshot can never delete a live reservation
The snapshot is applied to on_hand and the difference becomes a reported drift
Return restore: QC result vs RMA quantity
Only the received quantity with QC PASS is restored
The rest stays sold and remains reconcilable

nodes.title: Dedicated: Exception Handling and Compensation Strategy
nodes.intro_md: Two rules drive everything below. First, classify before you decide: a business rejection, a transient system fault and a data inconsistency need three different responses. Second, never leave a partial effect: if the second half of a two-step operation cannot complete, a named compensation job must own it within a stated SLA.

rows: Insufficient stock, off-shelf SKU, illegal state, quantity limit, RMA outside the return window

No 5xx for expected business conditions
Error responses contain no stack traces, SQL, internal hostnames or PII

cases.title: Client-supplied price or quantity is never trusted
precondition: A crafted createOrder request carrying amount = 0.01 for a 100.00 SKU
steps: Read the stored order amount and the payment intent
expected: The server recomputes the amount from SKU and promotion rules

The amount stored equals the amount charged in the later payment callback

cases.title: Payment callback write-back contract
precondition: A signed callback template with every documented field
steps: Deliver an amount mismatch, an unknown order_no, a bad signature, a missing pay_no and a duplicate pay_no
expected: Amount mismatch -> rejected, no state change, alert raised, callback acknowledged safely
Unknown order_no -> routed to the manual/exception queue, never auto-creating an order
Bad signature -> 401 with no mutation; duplicate pay_no -> idempotent success
Every callback outcome is visible in a metric with the reject reason

cases.title: WMS ship-notice write-back contract
precondition: A schema-valid and several schema-invalid ship notices
steps: Deliver: valid, missing tracking_no, illegal tracking_no format, package count not matching the shipped quantity sum, unknown so_id
Inspect order state, DLQ and alerts
expected: Valid notice applies fully and is idempotent per package
Invalid notices go to the DLQ with a reason and cause no state change
Unknown so_id is parked and alerted rather than creating a new order

cases.title: Stock synchronization message schema and version guard
precondition: E4/E5 messages with a missing version field, a future-major version and a wrong type on qty
steps: Read applied version, inventory and the DLQ
expected: A missing or unsupported version is rejected rather than guessed
Type errors are rejected at the boundary with a schema-error reason
Every accepted message is recorded with its version for traceability

cases.title: Query API limits and encoding
precondition: A large result set and adversarial inputs
steps: Request page_size = 0, -1, 100000; an unknown sort field; SQL/HTML fragments and emoji in address and remark; a 5,000-character remark
expected: Pagination is bounded by the documented cap and returns 4xx beyond it
Sort/field names are whitelisted; unknown values rejected
Unicode and emoji are stored and returned round-trip correctly; injection attempts are neutralized with no data disclosure

cases.title: Cancel/refund API validation and guards
precondition: Orders in PENDING_PAYMENT, PAID and SHIPPED states
steps: Cancel/refund each with: no reason code, an illegal reason code, a missing order_no, no permission
expected: State guard runs before any side effect
Reason code is validated against an enum and persisted
Permission failures return 403 without revealing order details

cases.title: Sensitive-data masking in responses, logs and messages
precondition: An order carrying a full phone number, a detailed address and an ID number
steps: Read the order via the API, the admin console and a raw log export; inspect the SO push payload and MQ messages
expected: Storefront/admin responses mask phone and ID; the full value is returned only to an authorized owner in an approved field

Outbound WMS messages carry only the fields the warehouse needs, not the full customer record

cases.title: No internal-field leakage from storefront responses
precondition: A normal order plus an order in an internal failure state
steps: Diff the response payload against the public contract schema

Contract tests fail the build when a non-contracted field is added

cases.title: Flash-sale burst causes zero oversell and zero invariant violation
precondition: Perf environment, 500-unit SKU, load generator ready with a synchronized start
steps: Continuously sample available/reserved/sold and the latency histogram
expected: No sample shows a negative bucket or available + reserved + frozen != on_hand - safety_stock

cases.title: Sustained peak does not degrade into a queue collapse
precondition: Perf environment at production-like topology
steps: Track queue depth, consumer lag and p99 over time
expected: Latency and error targets hold for the whole hold period

Auto-scaling (if configured) stabilizes without flapping

cases.title: Eight-hour soak shows no leak and no slow drift
precondition: 1.2x peak, steady mixed traffic with sync traffic included
steps: Sample RSS, GC pauses, connection pool, ledger/DB growth, inventory divergence hourly
expected: Memory growth bounded (< 5%); no FD/connection leak
Inventory diff does not grow with time
Error rate and latency stable between hour 1 and hour 8

cases.title: Breakpoint behavior fails closed, never corrupts
precondition: Ramp load past the system knee
steps: Increase load until the system degrades
Inspect state and error taxonomy at the knee
expected: Degradation appears as explicit business/system rejections with retryable codes
Zero state corruption: no oversell, no negative bucket, no partial ledger entry
Recovery to normal latency without a restart once load recedes

cases.title: Seeded drift classes are all detected and compensated within SLA
precondition: Five deliberate drifts seeded: paid-but-not-deducted, shipped-but-not-deducted, closed-but-reservation-alive, return-received-but-not-restored, lost callback
steps: Track detection time, repair time and the ledger entries produced
expected: All five are detected within the declared window and repaired exactly once
Each repair leaves an ADJUST/compensation ledger entry with a reason code and batch id
Invariants I1, I3 and I4 hold after the sweep; no drift recurs

cases.title: Circuit breaker and fail-fast under a WMS outage
precondition: WMS mock switchable to an outage
steps: Restore the WMS and observe recovery
expected: Circuit opens within the declared window; order creation returns the documented retryable/queue response rather than hanging
Payment callbacks continue to be processed (bulkhead verified)
After restore, the breaker closes, the backlog drains and reconciliation reports zero unexplained diff

cases.title: Timeout and retry produce no duplicate effect
precondition: A dependency configured to accept the request and then time out on the response
steps: Trigger the retry path for E1 (SO push) and for the reserve call
Compare the effective apply count on the dependency with the platform ledger
expected: The dependency applies the operation once; the platform ledger matches
Retry attempts and outcomes are visible in metrics; the DLQ is empty after the fixed path is used

cases.title: Message-order guarantees hold under a reordering storm
precondition: A stream of E5 events plus E2/E3 pairs shuffled with duplicates
steps: Compare final state with the expected final state computed from the source of truth
expected: Final state matches the expectation exactly
Duplicates and reordered messages leave no residue
DLQ is empty and the late-message metric reflects the discarded stale events only

cases.title: Every alert in the catalog fires on a synthetically injected condition
precondition: Alert rules deployed to the test environment with the production thresholds
steps: Inject each condition in turn (oversell simulation, sync stall, DLQ growth, stuck orders, lag)
Measure detection latency and check the notification content
expected: Each alert fires within its declared detection window with the correct severity
The payload names the SKU/warehouse/order and links to the relevant dashboard
No alert storm: a single incident produces one notification per severity, not per event

cases.title: Inventory diff ratio reflects a real divergence within one cycle
precondition: A synthetic divergence of 0.1% introduced for one warehouse
steps: Wait for the hourly diff job
Read the metric, the alert and the report
expected: The metric reports the divergence within the declared cadence
The alert fires at the configured threshold
The report lists the SKUs and deltas for triage

cases.title: Trace continuity across the storefront-WMS boundary
precondition: A single order driven end-to-end with the WMS mock
steps: Collect the trace ids for createOrder, reserve, callback, deduct, SO push, ship notice
Check the logs on both sides
expected: One searchable correlation id links the whole journey
Out-of-order arrivals are visible in the trace with timestamps proving the sequence
No PII appears in the traced payloads

cases.title: Stuck-order detection covers every non-terminal stage
precondition: One order artifically stalled in each non-terminal state
expected: Every stalled order is reported with its stage and dwell time
Grouping by stage matches the injected set exactly (no false negatives)
Alerts respect the threshold and do not fire on healthy orders

cases.title: Callback authenticity cannot be bypassed
precondition: Captured valid callbacks plus a signing key in the test store
steps: Attempt: no signature, wrong key, tampered amount, replayed nonce, expired timestamp, body/header mismatch
expected: Every attempt is rejected with no state mutation and an audit log entry
The rejection reason distinguishes auth failure from contract failure
Legitimate callbacks continue to succeed during the attack window (no denial of service from the guard)

cases.title: Privileged inventory adjustment requires authorization and leaves an audit trail
precondition: A normal user token and an admin token
steps: Attempt an ADJUST with the normal token
Perform one with the admin token and a reason code
expected: Normal token -> 403 with no change
Admin adjustment adds a ledger row with operator, ticket, reason and before/after values
A reversal produces a second auditable entry rather than deleting the first

cases.title: No PII in logs, metrics or outbound messages
precondition: An order carrying a full phone number, address and ID
steps: Scan logs, metric labels, traces and all outbound WMS/gateway payloads
expected: Zero unmasked PII occurrences (regex plus a checksum-based scan for ID numbers)
The outbound WMS message contains only warehouse-relevant fields
The CI gate fails the build if the scan regresses

cases.title: Release gate: dependency and image scan
precondition: The release candidate images and the SBOM
steps: Run the CVE scan and the secrets scan
expected: No high/critical vulnerability with an available fix ships with the release
No secret or key material is present in the repository or the image layers
Findings are recorded with an owner and an accepted-risk decision where deferred

cases.title: Database failover loses no order and no ledger entry
precondition: A production-like environment with a replica and the failover mechanism configured
steps: Let the failover complete, then compare state
expected: RTO within target; order and payment RPO = 0
No partially applied ledger entry and no orphan reservation
Invariants hold after recovery; the reconciliation reports zero unexplained diff

cases.title: Point-in-time restore reproduces known totals
precondition: A backup plus an agreed reference timestamp and its reported totals
steps: Restore into a sandbox and replay to the reference timestamp
Compare orders, payments and ledger sums
expected: Totals match the reference report exactly
Restore duration is recorded against the target
The procedure is executable by an on-call engineer from the runbook alone (no tribal knowledge)

cases.title: Stock recalibration from the WMS source of truth is safe and audited
precondition: A deliberately divergent SKU/warehouse
steps: Run the recalibration procedure with an approval record
Inspect the ledger, invariants and the SKU's sellable state
expected: Divergence is corrected with reason-coded ADJUST entries carrying the batch id
Invariants hold; the SKU returns to sellable if previously frozen
The approval record names the approver and the ticket

cases.title: Rollback of a release is verified, not assumed
precondition: The release candidate plus its predecessor image and the feature flags

Run the smoke and consistency checks
expected: Rollback completes within the window without a schema migration
Order/inventory consistency is preserved across the rollback
Any message produced by the new version remains consumable by the old one (schema compatibility verified)
